# A HOLE BELONGS TO ITS NEAREST ENCLOSING GENERATOR (ADR-005,
# 2026-08-26; use-cases/BUGS.md §34): an outer pack's fill pass used

# holes: the inner `_` is the inner generator's source child, both as

# (its own hole, the second, stays its own). The two-arg

# fill untouched. Parity-probed in both engines.

# A HOLE NOTHING BINDS. Each form below once took its value from a
# peer, the data or a container's meet; `&` meets and never fills a
# hole, so each is an error of the schema wherever the hole stands: a
# call or an operator met with a value, a hole alone or in a member, a
# pair of holes, a hole in a rider's record or under a seal, in a call's
# container argument, beside a path, under super, pref, refer or a
# bound, in a spread's template, in a size, a trial or a match, in an
# operand of `+`, and in a group.
# A NAME NOTHING USES holds its hole harmlessly, as the definition reads
# a declaration's body: what waits on the hole reads as what any value
# could make of it, so a call over the hole, a pair of holes, a hole met
# with a value, one in a call's list and one under a `+` stand. What is
# wrong whatever the hole takes is still wrong, and a seal or a rider
# around a container that holds one still refuses a key it doesn't name.
